result.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
result.summary: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 World In-Context Learning 范式与 RoboScript 基础设施：冻结模型从单条示范出发在仿真世界中演练任务，把世界反馈写入上下文而非权重，固化为 Task Memory 后在新场景部署；在 RoboTwin 2.0 的 50 个任务上无梯度更新取得 83.4% 平均成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「上下文中学到的是任务步骤与物体角色等语义、而非视觉外观」的观察，可能与 LVR 关注的视觉细节保留、信息坍缩以及外部反馈如何写入推理状态相关，但论文属机器人操作设定且不涉及 latent 推理，仅为可供核查的远邻线索。
